slides.title: Class Abstraction and Encapsulation

blocks.text: Class abstraction means to separate class implementation from the use of the class.
The creator of the class provides a description of the class and let the user know how the class can be used.
The user of the class does not need to know how the class is implemented. The detail of implementation is encapsulated and hidden from the user.

slides.title: Aggregation and Composition

blocks.text: Aggregation is a special form of association that represents an ownership relationship between two objects.

Aggregation models has-a relationships. The owner object is called an aggregating object and its class an aggregating class. The subject object is called an aggregated object and its class an aggregated class.
Composition is a special case of the aggregation relationship, where the aggregated object cannot exist on its own.

❑Composition is a special case of the aggregation relationship, where 
the aggregated object cannot exist on its own.

slides.title: Wrapper Classes

blocks.text: A primitive type is not an object. However, Java defines wrapper classes that allow you to process primitive data types as objects:
The instances of all wrapper classes are immutable. Their internal values cannot be changed once the objects are created.

slides.raw_text:
Wrapper Classes
❑A primitive type is not an object. However, Java defines wrapper 
classes that allow you to process primitive data types as objects:
➢ Byte 
➢ Short
➢ Integer 
➢ Long
➢ Float 
➢ Double
➢ Character 
➢ Boolean 
❑The instances of all wrapper classes are immutable. Their internal 
values cannot be changed once the objects are created.

slides.title: MAX_VALUE and MIN_VALUE Constants

blocks.text: Each numeric wrapper class has the constants:
MAX_VALUE represents the maximum value MIN_VALUE represents the minimum value
For Float and Double, MIN_VALUE represents the minimum positive (close to zero) float and double values.

slides.title: Parsing Strings into Numbers

blocks.text: Each numeric wrapper class has two static parse methods to convert a String into a numeric value.
The parseInt method in the Integer class parses a numeric String into an int value.
The parseDouble method in the Double class parses a numeric String into a double value.

slides.title: Checking Palindromes Ignoring

blocks.text: Here are the steps to solve the problem:
1. Filter the string by removing the non-alphanumeric characters. This is done by creating a StringBuilder object, appending only the alphanumeric characters, and returning a new filtered string.
You can use the Character.isLetterOrDigit(ch) method in the Character class to check whether character ch is a letter or digit.
2. Obtain a new string that is the reversal of the filtered string. Compare the reversed string with the filtered string using the equals method.
